svg.text: Where the books the codex is compiled from were written, and where this edition's witnesses come from.

g.data-desc: The Gospels and Acts (c. 70-100): the Passion, the parables, the Acts. The Life of Adam and Eve (1st c.): Adam, Eve, Seth and the branch.
g.text: Life of Adam and Eve, 1st c.

g.data-desc: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews (c. 75): the siege of Jerusalem. The Reversio sanctae crucis (7th-8th c.): Heraclius and the Cross. The Roman Missal and Martyrology (1570): the liturgy; 5,199 years to the Nativity.
The Protevangelium of James (2nd c.): Joachim and Anne.
Tertullian, Adversus Praxean (c. 210): sun, ray and the ray's tip.
The Apocalypse of Elijah (3rd c.): Elijah addressed by the word of the Lord.
Augustine, Quaestiones Evangeliorum (c. 400): the Samaritan's two pence.
Adso, On the Antichrist (c. 950): the birth of Antichrist.
Barlaam and Ioasaph (c. 1000): the apologue of the man in the well.
Michael and Satanael (11th-12th c.): the stolen robe, wreath and sceptre.
The Slavonic Book of Enoch (MSS 14th-18th c.): Enoch writes 360 books.
Voragine, the Golden Legend (c. 1260): the Rood, the Finding of the Cross, the saints.
The Wartburgkrieg (13th c.): a stone from Lucifer's crown.
The Council of Florence (1439): purgatorial punishments, no fire named.
The Debreceni codex (1519): Seth at Adam's grave, in Hungarian.
The Erdy codex (1526-27): the branch promised, the healing deferred.
The Teleki codex (1525-31): Adam alive when Seth returns.
Carion's Chronicle (1532): six thousand years, in three spans.
The Council of Trent (1562): the water mixed with the wine.
Caxton's Golden Legend (1483): the English the Legend is read in here.
The York, Chester, Towneley and N-Town plays (15th c.): the mystery cycles.
The Douay-Rheims Bible (1582-1610): the Catholic English of the Vulgate.
Suarez, De Angelis (1620): the angels' test, as theology.
Mary of Agreda, Mystical City of God (1670): the angels' test, as narrative.
Kalmany's folk tellings (1893): Elijah at the fall of the angels.
The Romanian carols of Judas (19th-20th c.): Judas plunders paradise.
Borgehammar's Reversio (2009): the Heraclius legend edited.

svg.text: what the compiler had, written before 1593
